reviewer: R1_editor (Handling Editor, Analytica Chimica Acta - desk re-screen, cycle 02 revision v3b)
summary: v3b is markedly more honest. The abstract, cover letter and conclusions now admit that the pilot's own CV error is the best level forecast and that 3 of 4 pre-specified hypotheses failed. 'Least biased' was withdrawn. The soil-only scope of the LOFO test and its source-level p = 0.64 are reported. Proposition 1 is correctly scoped and credited. The duplicated cover letter and the topic-selection record are gone, and submission figures are numbered correctly. The main oversell trigger from my first screen is therefore largely defused. The honesty, however, moves the desk risk from 'oversold' to 'insufficient quantifiable advantage'. No accuracy or decision endpoint favours B-RPM. FLAT is at least as good in the new reachability analysis. The compatible-set gate saves nothing. The new positive practical result ('a second batch helps every method') is close to a truism. One new unsupported claim appeared: gains better than power-law extrapolation (Table S1: Holm p = 0.222, source p = 0.383). Several technical-return items remain: author, CRediT, AI and funding placeholders; Supplementary Note 4 with an internal file path; 'review cycle 1', 'version-2', E-codes and 'S0' in the SI; 'identification set' still in Figures 5-6; garbled SI tables; inconsistent code-availability statements; 'six sources' vs eight; wrong section cross-references. The main text grew to about 11,000 words. The paper now fits ACA's critical-methodology genre (a theory-backed limitation plus a rigorous 38-task benchmark) better than its 'new method that works' genre. Its fate at the desk depends on whether the editor values the observability result on its own merits.
strengths: Transparent reporting of failed hypotheses and of FLAT's superiority on level now runs through the abstract, cover letter and conclusions, so the editor will not feel misled on the primary endpoint.

Proposition 1 is correctly scoped to the error path and credited against prior learning-curve theory and Dicker/EigenPrism, with a chemometric interpretation of the horizon. The theory section would now survive a statistically literate referee.
The scope of the cross-family test (soil only) and its source-level result are disclosed in Section 4.5.
The new per-task absolute-bias analysis and within-n0 information-fraction tertiles remove two confounded claims.
The SI was pruned from 43 to 22 tables, submission figures are numbered 1-8 to match the text, and the GA meets the minimum size.

issues.title: New unsupported headline claim: 'B-RPM forecast gains better than power-law extrapolation'
issues.description: The abstract, Introduction, Conclusions and cover letter now say that B-RPM predicted gains better than power-law extrapolation (and better than FLAT). Against IPL3 on the gain endpoint, the paper's own Table S1 shows +0.044, Holm p = 0.222, source level p = 0.383, 5/8 sources: not significant. Section 4.4 does not report the comparison at all. The FLAT gain comparison is significant at task level (Holm p = 0.001) but not at source level (p = 0.109, 6/8). The authors moved the method's advertised advantage from bias to gain while keeping an unsupported part of the claim. A referee who checks Table S1 will read this as a repeat of the cycle-02 oversell.
issues.evidence: Abstract ('It forecast gains better than the no-improvement rule and power-law extrapolation'); Conclusions; cover letter ('B-RPM predicted gains better than power-law extrapolation'); SI Table S1, row gain B-RPM vs IPL3: 0.044, task Holm 0.222, source p 0.383.
issues.corrective_action: Delete 'and power-law extrapolation' from every gain claim, or qualify it as 'not significant'. Report the B-RPM vs FLAT gain advantage with its source-level result (p = 0.109) in the abstract. The defensible B-RPM claim is narrower: better gain forecasts than FLAT and RPM at task level, and robustness of the level error to a non-soil prior on soil tasks.

issues.title: Terminology rename not propagated to figures and SI; SI tables render garbled in the PDF
issues.description: The text renamed 'identification set' to 'compatible set'. Figure_5 (legend 'Identification set (prior-free)') and Figure_6 (panel titles 'Truth inside identification set', 'Width of identification set') are byte-identical to the old files and still use the old term. In the Supplementary PDF, wide tables break column headers into fragments ('endp oint', 'BRPMLOF O', 'sourc ep') and scramble cell order (Table S1, the confirmatory-hypothesis table). An editor opening the SI sees an unprofessional, hard-to-read document.
issues.evidence: md5 Figure_5.png = Fig3_identification_set_examples.png and Figure_6.png = Fig5_observability.png; Supplementary_Material.pdf p. 1-2 (Table S1).
issues.corrective_action: Regenerate Figures 5 and 6 with 'compatible set'. Set the SI wide tables in landscape with fewer columns, splitting task-level and source-level results, and check the rendered PDF page by page.

issues.title: The new 'positive practical result' is close to a truism and, as framed, weakens the case for the method
issues.description: Highlight 5, the abstract's last result sentence and the cover letter present 'a second batch improved sample-size decisions more than any choice of forecaster' as the positive practical result. The staged arm uses N/4 instead of N/8 labelled samples, so the finding amounts to 'twice the data gives better decisions'. Total cost is not held equal and no cost-regret is computed. In the same table FLAT is at least as accurate as B-RPM in both arms, and the compatible-set gate never saves a batch. For an ACA editor deciding whether there is a methodological advance, ending the highlights on 'collect more samples, whichever forecaster you use' signals the opposite.
issues.evidence: Highlight 5; abstract; Section 4.6 paragraph 2; SI Table S15 (one-shot B-RPM 0.683/0.761, FLAT 0.740/0.759; staged B-RPM 0.781/0.836, FLAT 0.798/0.861; gated second-batch share 0.937/0.917).
issues.corrective_action: Replace Highlight 5 with a substantive finding (for example, 'Learning-curve slopes are set mainly by the noise floor, which a pilot cannot identify', or the IPL optimism result). Recast the staged analysis as a cost-aware comparison on existing outputs: at equal total reference budget, compare decide-now with an N/8 pilot, decide-after-second-batch, and fixed-n rules, by expected wasted reference analyses or regret. Report it as supporting evidence for the Proposition-1 recommendation, not as the main positive result.

R1E-C02-01.note: The abstract, cover letter and conclusions now state that FLAT is best on level (0.262 vs 0.282) and that 3 of 4 hypotheses failed, and the 'least biased' claim was withdrawn in favour of per-task absolute bias. That honesty removes the oversell, but the substance of the problem is now in plain view: no accuracy or decision endpoint shows B-RPM ahead. In the new reachability analysis FLAT matches or beats B-RPM (one-shot 74% vs 68% at N=400; staged 80/86% vs 78/84%), and RPM r=1 is also at least as good. The headline B-RPM claim about gains versus IPL3 is not significant (see NEW-01).

R1E-C02-02.note: Section 4.5 now says LOFO equals LOSO for non-soil families and reports source-level p = 0.641 and B-RPM-LOFO vs FLAT (worse, Holm p = 0.008). The abstract no longer attaches the p-value to the wrong comparison. However, Highlight 4 ('transfers across materials'), the abstract ('kept its accuracy with a prior from another application family'), the Introduction ('strictest transfer test available') and Section 4.5's causal conclusion ('Transferring structure rather than curves is the reason B-RPM generalises') still generalise a soil-only, task-level result. Multi-source non-soil data were not added; this is disclosed in review_02 but not in the Limitations list.

R1E-C02-03.note: A staged reachability analysis was added (Section 4.6, Tables S4, S14, S15). It shows that gating the second batch on the compatible set saves nothing (the set excluded the target in only 7% of cases; second-batch share 92-94%). The 'staged' arm decides from N/4 rather than N/8 samples, so the comparison confounds staging with simply having twice the data, and it is not cost-normalised. The result ('more data improves decisions for every method') is close to a truism and gives the compatible set or B-RPM no decision value.

R1E-C02-04.note: The proposition is now scoped to the expected CV/error path. Dicker/EigenPrism are described correctly (precision ~ sqrt(p)/n0) and prior learning-curve theory is credited, with a 'what Proposition 1 adds' sentence and a chemometric reading of kappa_0. Still missing: a worked real-task illustration of power hidden below the horizon.

R1E-C02-05.note: The 'first' claim was removed. Coverage is now paired with width in the abstract (but not in Highlight 3). Whole-curve coverage (86%) and long-horizon bias caveats were added, and 'identification set' was renamed 'compatible set'. Still open: (i) 'pre-registered' remains in the cover letter and text for an internal log; (ii) code availability is inconsistent: the cover letter says 'available to referees on request', the Data availability statement says 'provided as Supplementary Material', and Section 2.5 says 'committed to the project repository'; (iii) a new unsupported gain claim was introduced (NEW-01).

R1E-C02-06.note: Per-family behaviour is mentioned (B-RPM optimistic for soil, pessimistic for mixtures) and the Limitations state the soil dominance. The per-family table remains in the SI (S9), and the abstract still says 'spectroscopy' generally.

R1E-C02-07.note: Section 4.1 is unchanged: no kappa window for the 0.037 collapse SD, and no n-stratified theory error, although Fig. 2 still shows the small-n offset and the small-kappa fan-out.

R1E-C02-08.note: The cover letter is no longer duplicated, the topic-selection record was removed, and the main text no longer says 'after the first review cycle'. Still present: Supplementary Note 4 'Literature matrix and novelty map' with the internal path manuscript/refs/verified_refs.json; 'Version-1 results and review cycle 1 showed...' in Supplementary Note 2; 'sensitivity analysis S0' in the SI; E0-E8 codes (Table S21 title, Note 1); 'version-2 design' in Table S8, Figure S1 and Section 3.6 ('before any version-2 forecast', 'first-version outputs'). Author, affiliation, CRediT, AI-statement ('Authors: confirm or amend') and funding placeholders remain in the manuscript and cover letter.

R1E-C02-09.note: The SI was pruned from 43 to 22 tables, but the main text grew from about 10,300 to about 11,000 words (manuscript_v3b.txt). Table 2 still has 13 rows, the forecaster zoo is unchanged, and the three-stage design history remains in Section 3.6. review_02.md lists main-text trimming as 'pending'.

R1E-C02-10.note: The Introduction still says 'six public sources' while Section 3.7 says eight. Section 4.7 still cites 'Section 2.4' for the ablation finding, and Section 2.3 still says RPM-w is defined in 'Section 3.6'.

R1E-C02-11.note: Figure_1..8 submission copies now match the text numbering (checked by checksum), and the GA is 1328 x 531 px (meets the minimum). However, the GA plot is unchanged: B-RPM sits below the true curve at every n, and the power-law curve is flat and pessimistic, which contradicts the paper's 'IPL is optimistic' message. Fig. 5 still shows the Mango case where B-RPM is clearly worse than FLAT. Figures 5 and 6 still say 'identification set' (NEW-02).

desk_decision: Borderline, now leaning towards sending for review. As packaged it would still get a technical return (placeholders, internal material and version/review-cycle wording in the SI, figure terminology). After cleanup and removal of the unsupported gain claim I would send it out, framed as a theory-backed critical-methodology paper.
recommendation: Complete the technical cleanup, remove the remaining unsupported claims and reframe the paper around the observability limit before submission. All top changes can be made without new data collection. With them done, the estimated desk-reject probability falls to about 0.28-0.30. The residual risk is structural: the named method has no quantifiable advantage, and the multi-source non-soil transfer test cannot be added from existing data.
recommendation_rationale: Top remaining changes, ranked by impact on desk-rejection risk (none needs new data). (1) Finish the technical cleanup: delete Supplementary Note 4; purge 'review cycle 1', 'version-1/2', 'first-version', E0-E8 and 'S0' from the SI and Section 3.6; fill or explicitly mark all author, CRediT, AI and funding fields; make code availability consistent across the cover letter, Section 2.5 and Data availability; fix 'six sources', the 'Section 2.4' and 'Section 3.6' cross-references and the garbled SI tables; regenerate Figures 5-6 with 'compatible set'. These items alone trigger a technical return. (2) Remove the remaining unsupported or over-general claims: 'gains better than power-law extrapolation' (n.s.); 'transfers across materials' (Highlight 4) and 'strictest transfer test available' (soil only); 'Transferring structure ... is the reason B-RPM generalises' (causal, task-level only); and 'pre-registered' for an internal log. (3) Reframe the title, abstract and highlights so that the contribution is the observability limit plus the benchmark findings: pilot CV error is the best level estimate, IPL is systematically optimistic, slopes are set by the noise floor, and long extrapolations are undetermined. Present B-RPM as the tool that makes the unavoidable prior explicit, and replace Highlight 5 with a substantive finding. This positions the paper in ACA's critical-methodology tradition (cf. Olivieri 2025/2026, Saccenti & Camacho 2027) rather than as a method that loses to the trivial rule. (4) Recast the staged analysis on existing outputs as a cost-aware comparison at equal total budget (regret or wasted reference analyses), so the recommendation rests on a non-trivial result. (5) Cut the main text to 8,000 words or fewer: five forecasters in Table 2, the design history reduced to two sentences, RPM variants and ablations moved to the SI. The text has grown since cycle 02. (6) Redesign the GA as a schematic of horizon, compatible set and prior, or use an example where B-RPM tracks the truth and IPL is optimistic; add a sentence and panel showing, on one real task, power below the horizon that is invisible in the pilot but learned at large n (existing data). If the editor reads the paper primarily as a forecasting-method paper, it remains desk-rejectable on 'no advantage over existing approaches'. CILS or J. Chemometrics remain the fallback.
